meta.purpose: Ledger of specific news claims the nightly scanner has already verified as misdated (the underlying event is real, but its true date is a year or more away from the date implied by the aggregator/republication that surfaced it). Created for backlog item SC-1 / defect class DC-13, opened after the Meta '8,000 layoffs' claim and the China 'Ethnic Unity Law' claim each recurred and were re-verified from scratch across multiple nightly cycles, and after 8 of the 14 candidates dropped on the 2026-09-18 cycle turned out to be the same shape of error.
meta.brief_addendum: Before verifying a candidate's date from scratch, check research/known-misdated-claims.json for an active entry matching this entity. If one matches, you do not need to re-run verification searches -- cite the entry's true_date and source, drop the candidate as already-known, and append today's date to that entry's occurrences[] array (append-only; do not edit or remove prior entries). An entry means 'this specific claim is misdated', not 'this entity is banned' -- the same entity can and will produce genuine, correctly-dated news on a different topic, and that must still be flagged normally. validate-scan.mjs enforces this: it fails the scan if a top_entities candidate matches an active ledger entry's matcher, but a correctly-dropped candidate never triggers a failure.
meta.how_entries_are_read: See research/scripts/validate-scan.mjs, section 8 (checkKnownMisdatedClaims). Only entries with status 'active' are checked. A candidate is flagged when EVERY token-group in matcher[] has at least one substring hit (case-insensitive) against the concatenated slug+name+news_summary text of a research/scans/<date>.json top_entities item (see section 8c in validate-scan.mjs for exactly which fields of a candidate are read and why -- narrowed 2026-09-21, SC-1c, after a live run showed a candidate's own news_summary can quote ledger vocabulary while correctly explaining it is NOT a match).

claims.description: 'Meta cuts/lays off 8,000 jobs' is a real event, but it happened 2026-05-20, not in September. An undated aggregator snippet keeps getting re-surfaced as if it were new.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the 8,000-job cut is a fresh September 2026 announcement/execution.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Meta entity token AND the specific 8,000 headcount figure AND a job/layoff word, all three, regardless of phrasing order (e.g. 'cut 8,000 jobs' and '8,000 job cuts' both match). A genuine, differently-sized Meta layoff (e.g. 12,000 jobs) or a genuine Meta story with no layoff/job content will not match, because at least one required group is absent. The count group (8,000/8000) is the group doing the real specificity work here -- 'job'/'jobs' alone is broad, but combined with Meta AND the exact 8,000 figure it is not a realistic false-positive shape.
claims.source: research/scans/2026-09-17.json stats.dropped_candidates (meta-platforms (possible)); research/scans/2026-09-18.json stats.dropped_candidates (meta-platforms (possible)); research/digests/2026-09-18.md line 92 and 165 ('third consecutive cycle')
claims.notes: The 2026-09-18 digest and scan record both describe this as the claim's 'third cycle' / 'third consecutive cycle', but only two prior scan files (2026-09-17, 2026-09-18) are committed in research/scans/ with an itemized dropped_candidates record. No research/scans/2026-09-16.json exists. occurrences[] records only the two documented cycles; it is not stretched to three to match the prose claim.

claims.description: 'Interpublic Group cut 3,200 jobs, including 800 in September' is a real figure, but the 800-role tranche falls in the three months ended 30 September 2025 (Q3 2025, per SEC filing/reporting), a year stale relative to a September 2026 scan window -- part of a broader 2025 restructuring ahead of the Omnicom merger. Recurred without a ledger entry across the 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 cycles, costing a full verification search each time.
claims.true_date_reason: The 2026-09-21 scan's verification establishes only 'the three months ended 30 September 2025 (Q3 2025)' (SEC filing/reporting) for the 800-role tranche -- a quarter, not a specific day. No committed record gives a day-level date for when in that quarter the 800 roles were eliminated; recording null rather than guessing a day within Q3 2025.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the 800 September layoffs are a fresh September 2026 development, rather than the September-2025-ending Q3 tranche of a 2025 restructuring ahead of the Omnicom merger.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Interpublic Group entity token AND the specific 800-role headcount figure AND a job/layoff/cut token, all three. This is deliberately narrower than the entity name alone: a genuine, differently-sized Interpublic Group headcount story -- e.g. the ~15,000-role combined Omnicom/Interpublic Group headcount reduction reported 14 September 2026 (research/scans/2026-09-17.json, carried as context rather than flagged because its sourcing was undated -- an entirely different, undisputed-as-current story) -- uses the figure 15,000 and the word 'roles', not '800' and 'jobs'/'cut', and so will not match. A genuine Interpublic Group story with no headcount content also will not match.
claims.notes: The 2026-09-21 scan record explicitly flags this claim as unledgered for 'a second consecutive cycle' after 2026-09-20, and separately reports a genuine, differently-sized 15,000-role Omnicom/Interpublic Group headcount story (already noted above) that must not be confused with this claim. No committed record documents this specific 800-in-September claim recurring before 2026-09-20; occurrences[] reflects only the two documented cycles.

claims.description: Judge Allison Burroughs' ruling that the Trump administration's Harvard funding freeze was unlawful was issued 2025-09-03 (case docket, President and Fellows of Harvard College v. HHS, 1:25-cv-11048), a year stale relative to a September 2026 scan window. Multiple sources describe it only as 'September 3' without a year -- the exact shape of error this ledger exists to catch.
claims.claimed_framing: An undated 'September 3' mention is read as a September 2026 ruling rather than the actual 2025-09-03 decision.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Harvard entity token AND the presiding judge's surname ('Burroughs', a distinctive token not used in ordinary Harvard news) AND a funding-freeze/ruling token, all three. A genuine Harvard story that mentions Judge Burroughs on an unrelated docket she also presides over (e.g. the international-student visa litigation) without funding-freeze/ruling language will not match; nor will a genuine Harvard funding story that does not involve Burroughs at all.
claims.notes: Newly discovered on the 2026-09-21 cycle (research/scans/2026-09-21.json calls it 'NEWLY DISCOVERED MISDATED CLAIM (not yet in the ledger)'), bundled in the same scan record with the distinct Heightened Cash Monitoring claim below (harvard-heightened-cash-monitoring) but recorded as a SEPARATE entry rather than one combined entry: the two facts have different true dates (2025-09-03 vs ~2025-09-19) and this ledger's schema carries one true_date per entry, and each fact can plausibly resurface independently of the other (a future snippet could restate just the ruling, or just the HCM/letter-of-credit status, without the other). A single entry with an OR-style matcher across both topics could not honestly report a single true_date for whichever half actually matched, so two entries is the more accurate choice even though the scan record's own recommended matcher sketch ('harvard' + 'burroughs'/'heightened cash monitoring' + 'september') suggested one.

claims.description: Harvard's placement on the US Department of Education's Heightened Cash Monitoring (HCM) status, with a $36M letter-of-credit requirement, was reported 2025-09-19/2025-09-20 (Harvard Crimson, Inside Higher Ed) -- a year stale relative to a September 2026 scan window.
claims.claimed_framing: An undated report of Harvard's HCM/letter-of-credit status is read as a September 2026 development rather than the actual September 2025 placement.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Harvard entity token AND the distinctive 'Heightened Cash Monitoring' / letter-of-credit phrase (a specific US Department of Education status name), mirroring the 2-group precedent already used for china-ethnic-unity-law where the second phrase is itself distinctive enough not to need a third group. Genuine, unrelated Harvard funding or compliance news that does not use this specific status name will not match.
claims.notes: Same 2026-09-21 discovery as harvard-funding-freeze-ruling but a distinct fact with a distinct true_date (source states a 19-20 September 2025 range for the report; recording the earlier day, consistent with how this ledger's venezuela-maduro-captured and anthropic-pentagon-suit entries resolve a stated range to its earliest day) -- see harvard-funding-freeze-ruling's notes for the one-entry-vs-two-entries rationale.
